newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tigon leaps as shares recover losses.
newsitem.headline: Tigon leaps as shares recover losses.

text.p: South African electronics and financial services group Tigon Ltd continued its recovery on Wednesday as the company's woes seemed over, dealers said.
Tigon was knocked heavily over the past two weeks following its suspension on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on May 14 over the accounting of its 1996 financial results.
"I think it's (Tigon) over the bad news now. There is nothing wrong with the company, they just had to show how their earnings were made," one dealer said.
The share jumped 19.57 percent, or 135 cents, to 825 cents in thin volume.
Its suspension was lifted on May 16 after it said 17.9 million rand, or 54 percent of its income for the period, was based on a fee that was not due to be received until October.

"It think the market just knocked it (share) down on the news that came into the market...and there just has to be a correction. I think they are just going to consolidate at these levels for a while," another dealer added.
